results.disconfirmation_attempt: Reviewed the function: echoing the original requested key is a reasonable contract (caller gets back what they asked for), and deduplication by normalized value is intentional to avoid duplicate mbox reads. No test or caller in scope contradicts this; the behavior is self-consistent and documented as a single read-only pass.
results.evidence: targets: dict[str, str] = {}; for header_message_id in header_message_ids: target = normalize_message_id(header_message_id); targets[target] = header_message_id ... found[original] = _message_body(message); return found
results.expected_behavior: load_message_bodies should return a dict mapping each requested Message-ID (normalized) to its full body, loaded in a single read-only mbox pass.
results.suspected_violation: load_message_bodies keys the result dict by the caller's original (un-normalized) input string rather than the normalized Message-ID, and when multiple inputs normalize to the same value, the last request wins—potentially surprising callers who expect normalized keys.

results.disconfirmation_attempt: Traced the confirmation gate: position < 9 short-circuits (warmup), redundant short-circuits, and confirmed_pair requires previous.redundant plus current redundancy — matching the "two consecutive confirming actions after warmup" contract. Verified _near_duplicate handles tool name, read_file path+line-range overlap (≥0.5), and normalized-argument equality otherwise. Verified novelty=0.0 for empty evidence cannot exceed threshold. Serialization round-trip preserves the fields read by _extract_action. No counterexample produced.
results.evidence: assess_trajectory builds _Action list via _extract_action, computes novelty = len(evidence-seen)/len(evidence), flags duplicate via near-duplicate within a 12-action trailing window, and only issues an Intervention when position >= _WARMUP_TOOL_ACTIONS+1 and both current and previous actions are redundant. _serialize_action reproduces the input schema (index, _detector_sequence_offset, tool_call, tool_result.meta) so serialized assessments feed back in cleanly. All paths are internally consistent with the documented contract.
results.expected_behavior: A confirmed low-novelty action loop requires two consecutive redundant actions (duplicate and novelty ≤ 0.10) after the warmup boundary (zero-based position ≥ 9). The returned Intervention's truncation_point should mark the start of the repeated loop, and the detector should be live-versus-replay equivalent.
results.suspected_violation: No surviving defect found. The warmup boundary, redundancy confirmation, near-duplicate tool/read_file comparison, evidence-novelty computation, and serialization round-trip all trace consistently against the documented contract. The redundant second clause in confirmed_pair is harmless. No integrity, boundary, or contract violation survived the disconfirmation attempt.
